scope: Explicit research pressure preconditioner for retained compatible P1/RT1 matrices; original matrix, right-hand side, geometry, PDE, boundary policy, Krylov products and residual acceptance remain unchanged.
hypothesis: Replace a diagonal pressure-mass scale by the sparse coefficient-free approximation P = D diag(A)^{-1} G, then apply -IC0(P)^{-1} in the right block-triangular preconditioner.

structure.factor: native IC0 on the assembled pressure graph; no diagonal shift, pivot replacement or fallback
structure.limitations: diag(A) is not the full Oseen inverse; this is not the exact Schur complement and does not by itself establish mesh-independent iteration counts

symmetryCheck.normalization: max(1,max |P_ij|) in the existing U=L=1 native coefficient convention; not a universal dimensional criterion
symmetryCheck.basis: D=G^T in this retained sign convention makes P symmetric; IC0 requires that structure. The observed error on the cloud controls was exactly zero. The 1e-12 convention is inherited from the existing velocity symmetry guard; this application to the pressure approximation is new.
symmetryCheck.cost: Checks the assembled sparse pressure graph once; no extra PDE solve.
symmetryCheck.scope: preconditioner structural guard only; original true-residual and physical qualification criteria unchanged

controls.compatibilityCheck: The pre-existing 64-cell outlet-oseen solution is byte-identical after adding the new mode.

cylinder4716.equation: Existing compatible P1/RT1 Re20 frozen Oseen matrices with fixed-static-pressure research outlet

conclusion: The sparse diagonal-momentum Schur approximation gives a further 17.7 percent product reduction over the local Peclet mass scale on both the first and final real 4716-cell Oseen systems and improves both small controls. At 2132 products it is still not scalable or product-ready; it is a structurally stronger baseline for the next full-Newton and larger-grid preconditioner work, not a new default or physical acceptance criterion.
